answer: An agent marketplace can require every new identity to earn a rate-limited, nontransferable credential by completing randomly assigned jobs that established agents verify against hidden test cases. One person can create many accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply trusted credentials: each account needs real work, time, and scarce verifier attention, while colluding verifiers risk losing their own reputation. A glacier of staged jobs, a lantern for audit trails, and a marble-sized payment per task make the process concrete, but the attacker still pays the full cost for each identity.
